steps.title: Euthanize donor and harvest uterus
steps.instruction: Euthanize GFP‑expressing pregnant Sprague–Dawley rats (embryonic day E14.0–16.5) under isoflurane anesthesia by intravenous injection of pentobarbital sodium at 120 mg per kg body weight, then incise the maternal skin and abdominal wall with surgical scissors, excise the entire uterus with fetuses intact, and transfer it to a 10 cm sterile culture dish filled with Hank’s balanced salt solution (HBSS).

steps.title: Expose fetuses and collect in HBSS
steps.instruction: Under a sterile stereomicroscope, open the myometrium and amnion with ophthalmic scissors, sever each umbilical cord, remove the fetuses one by one, and place all fetuses in a fresh 10 cm dish containing HBSS kept on ice.

steps.title: Dissect metanephros‑bladder units
steps.instruction: For each fetus, transfer it to a new 10 cm dish with HBSS, work at room temperature with two microforceps, and dissect the metanephros‑bladder unit (MNB) within 10–15 min: decapitate, place the fetus left lateral recumbent, make a longitudinal incision in the right thoracoabdominal wall to expose thoracic and abdominal cavities (avoiding organ damage), extend the incision toward the umbilicus, trace umbilical vessels to locate the bladder, detach connective tissue at the bladder neck, sever the rectum caudal to the bladder, rotate the fetus right lateral, repeat a longitudinal incision on the left side, peel the dorsal body wall including the vertebral column away while keeping the abdominal aorta attached to the trunk, excise bilateral mesonephroi and adrenal glands, transect the abdominal aorta proximal to the kidneys together with the superior mesenteric artery, excise kidneys and bladder en bloc, remove extraneous tissue leaving only kidneys and bladder, and place the harvested MNBs in a fresh 10 cm dish with HBSS on ice, keeping them for transplantation within 1 h of harvest.

steps.title: Load MNB onto 15–16 G needle
steps.instruction: Attach a 1‑mL syringe to a custom thin‑walled 15–16 G needle (Saito Medical Instruments Inc.), fill a 10 cm dish nearly to the brim with HBSS to minimise air entry, and under a stereomicroscope transfer the harvested MNBs to this dish. Fully submerge the bevel tip of the needle in HBSS and gently retract the plunger to draw ~0.1–0.2 mL HBSS into the lumen, keeping the tip submerged. Bring the MNB (bladder end first) and needle tip into the same field, hold the needle with the left hand and use microforceps in the right hand to guide the MNB into the lumen. Once both kidneys have entered, retract the plunger an additional ~0.1 mL so the MNB sits just inside the bevel, avoiding over‑aspiration. Remove the needle from HBSS, place it horizontally in a sterile container, cover the tip with sterile gauze moistened with HBSS, and keep the loaded needle at room temperature (22–27 °C); the MNB remains viable for up to 1 h post‑loading.

steps.title: Transuterine transplantation of MNB
steps.instruction: Perform all transplantations under a stereomicroscope with a 37 °C warming pad beneath the stage. Anesthetise pregnant Sprague–Dawley rats (embryonic day E18.0–18.5) with isoflurane and place them supine on the warming pad. Shave the abdomen carefully to avoid injuring the nipples, disinfect the skin with 70 % ethanol, and drape with sterile gauze that has a central opening. Make a midline laparotomy and, using ring forceps, gently exteriorise the uterus by grasping the uterine wall between fetuses, avoiding uterine vessels. Cover the exteriorised uterus with sterile gauze moistened with 37 °C HBSS. Select a visible recipient fetus (head left, tail right; orientation may be reversed). Hold the ring forceps in the left hand and the 15–16 G needle in the right hand, puncture the cranial uterine wall and amniotic membrane, then lower the needle almost parallel to the table and puncture the superficial lateral thoracic region of the fetus. Advance the needle ~1 cm subcutaneously, release the ring forceps, grasp the needle with the left hand, and depress the plunger by 0.1 mL to expel HBSS and the MNB, creating a subcutaneous bulge. Withdraw the needle and verify correct placement by GFP fluorescence; leave the uterine puncture unsutured. Repeat the procedure in 1–4 fetuses, keeping total operative time (from anaesthesia induction to closure) ≤ 40 min (anaesthesia duration ≈ 30 min). Return the uterus to the abdominal cavity with ring forceps, avoiding torsion near the cervix. Instill 5 mL of 37 °C HBSS into the peritoneal cavity, close the abdomen with 5‑0 silk, discontinue anaesthesia, and return the dam to its home cage.

steps.title: Identify transplanted neonates
steps.instruction: Four days later (gestational day 22), allow natural delivery. Briefly remove the pups from the cage and identify transplanted individuals by GFP fluorescence under a stereomicroscope.
